nba_directive.reason_text: This client is sitting at 6.62% on a conventional loan and paying $41/month in PMI that builds zero equity — they're a textbook rate-and-term refi candidate who likely believes they need to wait for the Fed to move before acting. The Fed-vs-mortgage education is the highest-leverage opener here because it directly dismantles the 'waiting for rates' objection before it hardens.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Lead with the Fed-vs-mortgage education to reset their mental model
  - Open with something like: 'Quick thing worth knowing — mortgage rates don't actually follow the Fed rate. They track the 10-year Treasury, and any expected Fed cuts are already priced into today's mortgage market. Waiting for a Fed move may not move your rate the way you're thinking.'
  - This reframe is your door-opener; deliver it before quoting any numbers

- Anchor hard to their exact current rate of 6.62% and quantify the gap
  - Pull today's best achievable rate for their profile and state it explicitly
  - Show the gap: 'You're at 6.62% — here's where you could land today'
  - Compute the new principal & interest payment at the achievable rate and present the side-by-side: current P&I $1,575/mo vs. new P&I [calculated figure]
  - State the monthly savings in real dollars so the number is concrete, not abstract

- Layer in the PMI as a second source of monthly savings
  - Name it directly: 'You're also paying $41/month in PMI — that's money that doesn't reduce your balance by a single dollar'
  - Check their remaining balance of $232,268 against the original appraised value: if current LTV is at or near 80%, a refi appraisal may eliminate PMI at closing
  - If LTV is still above 80%, quantify how far they are from the drop-off threshold and flag it as a near-term milestone
  - Total monthly relief = payment reduction + $41 PMI savings — present the combined figure

- Run the break-even math to counter any residual 'I'll wait' instinct
  - Estimate closing costs for a rate-and-term refi on a $232,268 balance (typical range; use your shop's actual fee schedule)
  - Break-even = closing costs ÷ total monthly savings — present in months, not years, so it feels tangible
  - Frame it: 'If you break even in [X] months, every month after that is money back in your pocket — and waiting costs you that runway'

- Anchor to their specific financial pain, not a generic refi pitch
  - Tie the savings directly to whatever they've signaled matters: lower payment, getting out of PMI, certainty on their rate
  - Avoid any cash-out language — this is a rate-and-term conversation only

- Secure a concrete next step before closing the text
  - Offer a 10-minute call to run their exact numbers live, or send an e-consent link for a soft credit pull so you can quote with precision
  - Give them a specific ask: 'Can I pull a soft credit check — no impact to your score — so I can show you the exact payment and break-even for your file?'
  - Do not go silent after one message; if no reply in 24 hours, follow up with the break-even number as the hook
